claims.text: Silica (SiO2) can be used as a material for studying lattice heat conductivity modified by SRO precipitates.
Controlled introduction of SRO precipitates into silica will enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering from SRO precipitates will reduce phonon mean free paths in silica.
Introducing SRO precipitates will decrease the lattice thermal conductivity of silica relative to pristine silica.
Pristine silica has minimal microstructural inhomogeneity.
Electronic heat conduction is negligible in pristine silica.
SRO precipitates can be introduced into silica through tailored thermal treatments.
SRO precipitates can be introduced during sol-gel synthesis by dopant incorporation.
At room temperature or above, phonon-phonon interactions dominate thermal transport in the proposed silica system.
Electronic contributions to heat transport remain negligible under the proposed measurement conditions.
The density, size, and spatial distribution of SRO precipitates are the relevant structural mediators.
SRO precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon scattering times lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Modified silica will exhibit a statistically significant reduction in lattice thermal conductivity relative to pristine silica.
Modified silica will show evidence of reduced phonon scattering times.
The conductivity effect will occur predominantly where phonon transport dominates.
Uncontrolled precipitate concentration or other significant scattering mechanisms may cause deviations from the predicted effect.
The magnitude of conductivity reduction depends on precipitate size, concentration, and distribution.
